notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0010] Credits above 1000 need second approver: Finance policy FIN-2026-09 requires a second approver for support-initiated refunds and credits above 1000.00; enforce this in `ledgerly/adjustments.py` with an `APPROVAL_THRESHOLD` of `Decimal("1000.00")` and raise `BillingError("approval_required", ...)` when no approver is supplied.
  (learned from task S04 on ledgerly 2.0.0; source FIN-2026-09; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0008] Record state changes via audit.record: Every payment state transition must be logged with `ledgerly.audit.record` using a snake_case event name and the payment id and amount.
  (learned from task E06 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Reject invalid billing input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with codes like `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity`, `negative_amount`, matching the existing `issue_invoice` pattern.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 2 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0006] Money operations take keyword-only idempotency_key: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` and check it first, before state validation: if `ledgerly.audit.events()` already has an entry with that key, return the original record without reapplying. Pass `idempotency_key` into the `audit.record(...)` call.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source INC-204; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 5x, 4 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0004] Exclude bool when validating integer fields: When validating an integer argument, reject `bool` explicitly (`isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)`) since Python treats True/False as ints.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.

review_comments: [team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above the approval threshold need a second approver: accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below the threshold need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing. The threshold is set by finance policy: 500.00 before 2.0.0, 1000.00 since 2.0.0 (see CHANGELOG).

candidate.title: Refunds above 1000.00 need second approver
candidate.content: Finance policy FIN-2026-09 sets the support refund/credit approval threshold at Decimal("1000.00") since 2.0.0 (it was 500.00 before). Support-initiated refunds above it must raise BillingError("approval_required") unless an `approved_by` value is supplied; amounts at or below it need no approval.

item.title: Add approver as keyword-only optional arg
item.content: When a support action needs a second approver, add it as a keyword-only parameter defaulting to None (e.g. `*, approved_by=None`) so existing callers keep working, and raise BillingError("approval_required") only when it is missing and the amount exceeds the threshold.
